messages:
ashok: Heads-up — I ran a 30min load run on the new batching heuristic and saw a regression when prefix cache hits are high. latency P95 up ~12% for short-chat workloads.
elaine: Oof. repro steps?
ashok: repro is in the `continuous-batcher` branch. simple script: `./tools/load_test --model rdx-3b-q8 --qps 80 --mix short_chat:0.8,long:0.2`
jonathan: can you paste the profiler snap? even a tiny flamechart text helps.
ashok: paste:```
KV cache hit ratio: 72%
avg tokens/request: 24
effective batch length (tokens): 38
kernel chosen: matmul_small_opt (latency overhead: +1.8ms per batch)
context switch overhead: 0.9ms
queue wait: +3.4ms (spike at 11:22:13)
```
ashok: root cause hypothesis: when many requests are prefix-hit, they reduce incremental token budget which confuses token-budget-based packer. packer creates many narrow batches (many small requests) so kernel selection skews to small-kernel which has worse throughput at our GPU config.
kevin: that matches we saw with RT-cache experiment last month. small kernels have higher kernel-launch cost and less matmul amortization.
elaine: possible mitigations? pad to a min effective token budget? enforce a per-batch token floor?
jonathan: options: 1) pad hit requests to a min token count when forming batch (cheap), 2) prefer kernel selection by predicted throughput not just batch token total, 3) queue reordering to coalesce hit+miss pairs.
ashok: I prototyped (1) and (3). padding to 32 tokens reduced P95 by 6% but increased median cost by ~3%. reordering (put a small miss behind a hit) reduced kernel-switches by 40% and P95 improved 9% but adds complexity in fairness.
perf-bot: perf-alert: experiment "prefix-aligner-v1" ended. delta P95: -9% vs baseline on short_chat mix. cost delta +2.7% on tokens.
kevin: tradeoffs expected. We need an SLO-safe default. Maybe a hybrid: soft-pad to 24 tokens and weakly prefer coalescing into same kernel type.
elaine: agree. also add telemetry: emit `batch_kernel`, `batch_eff_tokens`, `kv_hit_frac` per batch to console so we can trace.
jonathan: we should also tie kernel selection to expected token density distribution. If batch has >60% hits, pick bulk-kernel that favors fewer kernel-launches even if per-op slightly worse.
ashok: I'll push a RFC PR describing: heuristics, metrics to add, two optional mitigations (pad floor + reorder window), and a small perf run plan.
kevin: please include the config knobs: `min_effective_tokens`, `reorder_window_ms`, `prefer_throughput_kernel_threshold`.
elaine: and add a canary in staging with synthetic 80% hit workload. I can run overnight. :thumbsup:
ashok: thanks — will open PR and tag @elaine @jonathan for review.
jonathan: nice work. make sure fallback to current packer if memory pressure spikes.
ashok: noted. will include safety checks and feature flag.
perf-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed: prefix-aligner-v1 -> staging @ 01:10 UTC
kevin: cool, let's watch metrics tomorrow morning.
